title: Alpha2 integer-count confirmation
research_question: Does frozen Alpha2 confirm at least a one-correct-classification-per-100 advantage over Alpha1 when the decision uses integer prediction counts?
hypothesis: Across the same 10 seeds and full TRAIN protocol, Alpha2 will achieve at least 10 more correct Q.ANT classifications over 1,000 TEST predictions than Alpha1 without increasing accuracy standard deviation by more than 0.01 absolute.
frozen_models: Alpha1: 12 local 8->4 Fourier/KAN blocks; 48->2 Fourier/KAN head
Alpha2: 12 local 8->8 Fourier/KAN blocks; 96->2 Fourier/KAN head

data_protocol.rule: Use unchanged Exp006 full-TRAIN protocol. No architecture, hyperparameter, preprocessing, seed, or epoch change.

primary_metric: Aggregate integer correct Q.ANT TEST predictions across 10 seeds (1,000 predictions per model).
success_criteria: Alpha2 must produce at least 10 more correct Q.ANT classifications than Alpha1 across 1,000 aggregate TEST predictions, and Alpha2 Q.ANT accuracy standard deviation must be no more than 0.01 absolute above Alpha1.
arithmetic_rule: Primary improvement gate MUST use integer correct-count difference >= 10, not floating-point mean accuracy arithmetic.
promotion_rule: If both frozen criteria are met, promote 8->8 to active PNN-v1 Alpha2; otherwise retain Alpha1.
hardware_boundary: Software/simulation-backend experiment only; no real photonic hardware performance claim.
